[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]

== Biography ==
'''William Glasgow''' is represented by a profile whose baptism details have not yet been resolved. Scotland's People separately indexes WILLIAME GLASGOW on 28 September 1648 in Glasgow parish, with parents WILLIAME GLASGOW and BESSIE HOWIE (OPR 644/1, reference 40/156).<ref name="SP1648">National Records of Scotland, Church of Scotland Old Parish Registers, births and baptisms, Glasgow parish 644/1, reference 40/156, WILLIAME GLASGOW, indexed 28 September 1648, parents WILLIAME GLASGOW and BESSIE HOWIE; Scotland's People index, original register page not inspected.</ref> A separate 24 October 1641 entry for William, son of [[Glasgow-992|William Glasgow]] and [[Howie-1119|Bessie Howie]], belongs to [[Glasgow-1497]]. The 1648 index supports this child's event and recorded parent names, but does not distinguish a birthday from a baptism date or establish later life or the exact identities of the attached parent profiles. The attached [[Glasgow-1497|William Glasgow]] is retained as a possible older sibling, but the claim that he died before this William's birth depends on the unresolved 1648 identification.

=== Early Life in Scotland ===
William's profile belongs in the context of mid-17th-century Scotland, a period of political and religious upheaval. No record inspected so far details his early life, proves that his family were Covenanters, or proves that he migrated to Ulster. The 1648 index places a child of this name and parent names in Glasgow parish, but the original page has not been inspected for a more precise location or context.


=== Possible connection to the Tyrone family ===

A late family history says that an ancestor named William Glasgow came from Scotland in connection with the 1689 relief of Londonderry and remained in northern Ireland.<ref name="WMG">William Melanchthon Glasgow, ''History of the Glasgow Family'', [https://www.wikitree.com/photo/pdf/Glasgow-590 PDF attached to Glasgow-590].</ref> It does not name that William's parents, baptism, exact Scottish parish or military unit. It also does not mention Glasgow High Kirk, Cavers, the 1679 prisoner transport or the Orkney wreck.

No parish, military, land, testament or other contemporary record has been found connecting the child represented by this profile to [[Glasgow-591]], [[Glasgow-551]] or the Tyrone family. The identification is therefore an unproved hypothesis, not a biography fact.

=== Two indexed entries ===

An earlier footnote wrongly combined this child's 1648 entry with the 1641 entry assigned to [[Glasgow-1497]]. Scotland's People lists the children separately: 24 October 1641, Glasgow OPR 644/1, reference 30/298, and 28 September 1648, Glasgow OPR 644/1, reference 40/156. The 1641 FamilySearch citation has been removed from this profile. The asserted “Vol. 3/3621” wording and guardians John Stewart and Michael Leckprivick still require the original 1648 register page; those details are not established by the index.

== Research Notes ==
=== Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

This dated review supersedes any earlier grade of this pair within the stated record scope. The existing father [[Glasgow-992]] is assessed at 98% (proved). Williame’s Glasgow child entry dated 28 September 1648 names Williame Glasgow and Bessie Howie. The full William/Bessie couple and exact 1648 Glasgow child event match the selected record father.

Confident for the baptismal child’s parentage; identification with the 1673 Quothquan testator remains working and does not inherit this confidence.

Next useful test: Test the Quothquan identity with the testament’s occupation, kin and place evidence.

Source basis already held: [https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Glasgow-1521 National Records of Scotland, Church of Scotland Old Parish Registers, births and baptisms, Glasgow parish 644/1, reference 40/156, WILLIAME GLASGOW, indexed 28 September 1648, parents WILLIAME GLASGOW and BESSIE HOWIE; Scotland's People index, original register page not inspected.]. No new father attached; cited evidence and any inspected register entry are scoped above.



* The 28 September 1648 date is independently indexed, but the index alone does not say whether it is a birth or baptism date. The structured birth date remains marked uncertain.
* The 1648 index names William Glasgow and Bessie Howie as parents of the indexed child. The exact identities of the attached parent profiles and any connection to the later Tyrone man remain unproved.
* The disputed 1648 note gives reference “Vol. 3/3621” and names John Stewart and Michael Leckprivick, but those details remain unverified.
* The only evidence offered for migration to Ireland is the late family narrative, which does not identify this child.
* Future research should locate the complete Glasgow High Kirk index entry or original register image before pursuing Tyrone records.

=== Quothquan testament, 1673 ===

A William Glasgow “in Quodquen” (Quothquan), Libberton parish, Lanarkshire, had a testament entered in the Lanark Commissary Court on 9 April 1673, register CC14/5/9.<ref name="Quothquan1673">Francis J. Grant, ed., ''The Commissariot Record of Lanark: Register of Testaments, 1595–1800'' (Edinburgh: Scottish Record Society, 1903), printed p. 38, entry “Glasgow, William, in Quodquen,” [https://www.tradeshouselibrary.org/uploads/4/7/7/2/47723681/the_commissariot_record_of_lanark__register_of_testaments__1595-1800_~_1903.pdf#page=50 digital copy]. The original testament, NRS CC14/5/9, images 24–26, was reviewed on 10 September 2026; the surviving selective reading finds no securely identified kin.</ref> He had died by that date. The index does not state his age, occupation, spouse, children or parents.

The former [[Glasgow-3912]] represented this Quothquan man and was merged into this profile as the leading existing-profile identification. A person baptised at Glasgow in 1648 could have lived at Quothquan and died by 1673, and no closer same-name candidate has been identified in the reviewed local cluster. The index gives no direct link to this profile's 1648 baptism or William and Bessie Howie. The combined identity is therefore a working inference, not a proved parent-to-testator chain. The original testament was reviewed on 10 September 2026. Its partly obscured opening and selective reading have not yielded a secure kin bridge to the 1648 Glasgow baptism; further reading may test the match. This Lanark record supplies no evidence of migration to Tyrone.
